lines.japanese: 虫の報せというやつだろうか。
lines.english: Maybe it was one of those gut feelings.

lines.japanese: 電車が柳木原へ向かっているあいだ、何故だか俺は、妙に落ちつかない気分だった。
lines.english: For some reason, as the train carried me toward Yanagihara, I felt strangely ill at ease.

lines.japanese: だから夜の上りの車内には空席がいくらでもあったのに、腰を下ろさず、なんとなくドアにもたれていた。
lines.english: So although the inbound train had any number of empty seats at that hour, I stayed on my feet, leaning absently against the door.

lines.japanese: ２２時を過ぎていた。
lines.english: It was past ten.

lines.japanese: 改札を出て駅東口から外へ出ると、ヤナポリ広場の群衆は静かに色めきたっていた。
lines.english: When I emerged from the station’s east exit, the crowd in Yanapoli Plaza was quietly agitated.

lines.japanese: 最初は芸能人やテレビカメラでも来てるのかと思った。しかし近付くにつれ、ひとびとの好奇を誘っているのは期待や興奮ではなく、もっと重苦しい──不安や同情のようなたぐいのものであると分かった。
lines.english: At first, I thought a celebrity or a television crew had appeared. But as I drew closer, I realized that what had caught everyone’s curiosity was not anticipation or excitement but something heavier: anxiety, pity.

lines.japanese: 往く者も来る者もみな一様に、同じ方向へ首を曲げ、目を投じている。その視線の先は、俺の馴染みの場所だった。
lines.english: Everyone passing in either direction had craned their necks toward the same place. Their gazes converged on a spot I knew well.

lines.japanese: ……いやな予感がした。
lines.english: ...I had a bad feeling.

lines.japanese: 俺は雑踏を掻きわけ、その深部へ潜っていった。
lines.english: I shouldered through the crowd and burrowed toward its heart.

lines.japanese: 「銃声」「撃たれた」「黒人が」「連続通り魔」「きのうの事件と関係が」
lines.english: “A gunshot.” “Somebody got shot.” “A Black man.” “A serial attacker.” “Maybe it’s connected to what happened yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 耳に触れる確証のないざわめきが胸を騒がせる。
lines.english: The unsubstantiated fragments reaching my ears set my heart racing.

lines.japanese: ひとの壁が厚くなってゆくのに比例して、身を震わす焦燥感のようなものが膨らんでゆく。俺は乱暴なぐらいの腕力で、強引に野次馬の壁をこじ開けて進んだ。
lines.english: The thicker the wall of bodies became, the more the urgency inside me swelled until I shook. I forced a path through the spectators with something close to brute force.

lines.japanese: 最後の障害は、体をこちらへ向けて両手を広げる警察官の姿だった。
lines.english: The final obstacle was a police officer facing me with both arms spread.

lines.japanese: そいつを隔ててその先で開けている空間には、ものものしい表情をした同じ制服がもうふたり。レンガ模様の路面には、脚の高いテーブルが横倒しになっていた。
lines.english: Beyond him, in the space held open, stood two more officers in the same uniform, their faces grave. A tall cocktail table lay on its side across the brick-patterned pavement.

lines.japanese: 転がった細長いトランクがぱっくり口を開け、鮮血色をしたビロードの内装が冬の夜に曝けだされている。その周囲にはマルチネス自慢の銀細工が散乱していた。
lines.english: A fallen oblong trunk gaped wide, exposing its blood-red velvet lining to the winter night. Martinez's treasured silverwork lay scattered around it.

lines.japanese: そして、ゆうべプラチナがたわむれに断末魔をあげたあの場所に、サスペンスドラマの血糊なんかよりよっぽど嘘くさく見える、黒ずんだ染みが広がっていた。
lines.english: And where Platinum had playfully performed his death agony the night before, a dark stain spread across the ground—looking far less real than stage blood in a television thriller.

lines.japanese: 俺は大きく息を吸って目を転じた。さらにその先の車道際にパトカーが一台停まっていて、そばで警官のひとりが、崩れそうな少女の体を両手で支えていた。
lines.english: I took a deep breath and tore my gaze away. Farther on, beside the road, a patrol car stood parked. An officer held up a girl who looked ready to collapse.

lines.japanese: 「アリス！」
lines.english: “Alice!”

lines.japanese: 俺は青い目をうつろに下向かせている少女の名を呼んだ。そして、列の先頭にいた警官の声と手が引きとめるよりも早く、そいつの元へ走った。
lines.english: I called to the girl with the vacant blue eyes. Before the officer at the head of the line could stop me—by word or hand—I ran to her.

lines.japanese: 「おい、入ってきちゃ駄目だ。戻りなさい！」
lines.english: “Hey! You can't come in here. Get back!”

lines.japanese: アリスを支えていた男が声を荒げた。それでようやくガキは俺に気付いたようだ。弾かれたように顔をあげ、母国語で支離滅裂に悲痛な叫びをあげた。
lines.english: The man holding Alice raised his voice. Only then did the kid seem to notice me. Her face snapped up, and she cried out in her native language, anguished and incoherent.

lines.japanese: 「君……知り合いか？」
lines.english: “You... know her?”

lines.japanese: 男が俺と異国の子供を交互に見た。俺はぞんざいに頷きながらアリスの正面で膝をつき、小さな肩を掴んでいた警官の腕を払いおとして優しく触れた。
lines.english: The man looked from me to the foreign child and back. I nodded curtly, knelt in front of Alice, brushed aside the officer’s arms, and gently laid my own hands on her small shoulders.

lines.japanese: 「アリス、どうした。大丈夫か」
lines.english: “Alice. What happened? Are you all right?”

lines.japanese: 「ジム……さされた……」
lines.english: “Jim... stabbed...”

lines.japanese: アリスが日本語で答えた。青い目が揺れて、たちまち涙が滲んだ。
lines.english: Alice answered in Japanese. Her blue eyes trembled, and tears welled in them at once.

lines.japanese: 「ジム、刺された！」
lines.english: “Jim was stabbed!”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫、聞いてる。うん。マルチネスが刺されたのか」
lines.english: “It's okay. I hear you. Martinez was stabbed?”

lines.japanese: 聞きかえすと、アリスは震えながら大きく頷いた。俺は自分の手に握力がこもるのを感じて、静かに息を吐いた。警官が先を促すように顔を近づけてきたが無視した。
lines.english: Alice gave a great, trembling nod. I felt my grip tighten and slowly breathed out. The officer leaned closer, urging her to continue, but I ignored him.

lines.japanese: 「なんで刺されたんだ」
lines.english: “Why was he stabbed?”

lines.japanese: 「私は分からない。とつぜん男は向けた、はものを私に」
lines.english: “I don't know. Suddenly, man point knife at me.”

lines.japanese: 「ジムはかばった私を……そしてジムはたおれた……」
lines.english: “Jim protect me... Then Jim fall...”

lines.japanese: 「かばって……刺された……？」
lines.english: “He shielded you... and got stabbed...?”

lines.japanese: なんだ。
lines.english: What.

lines.japanese: なんだ、これは。
lines.english: What was this?

lines.japanese: なにがどうなってるんだ。アリスが、こんな罪もないガキが、誰に狙われたって言うんだ。
lines.english: What the hell was going on? Who would target Alice—an innocent kid who had done nothing to anyone?

lines.japanese: 「マルチネスはどうした」
lines.english: “What happened to Martinez?”

lines.japanese: 「きゅきゅしゃ行った……」
lines.english: “Ambulance... take him.”

lines.japanese: 「救急車で先に搬送した」
lines.english: “They took him to the hospital in an ambulance.”

lines.japanese: 警官が補足するように小声で口を挟んだ。
lines.english: The officer quietly filled in the rest.

lines.japanese: 「後ろから深く刺されて危険な状態だった。この子にも付き添うよう勧めたけど、ドラを待つと言って聞かなかったんだ。ドラっていうのは君か」
lines.english: “He was stabbed deep in the back and was in critical condition. We urged the girl to go with him, but she wouldn’t listen. Said she had to wait for Dra. Are you Dra?”

lines.japanese: 俺は答える代わりにアリスへ尋ねた。
lines.english: Instead of answering, I asked Alice:

lines.japanese: 「どうした。なんで俺を待ってた」
lines.english: “What is it? Why were you waiting for me?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、逃げろ。ドラ、きけん」
lines.english: “Dra, run. Dra in danger.”

lines.japanese: アリスはたどたどしい命令形で訴えた。
lines.english: Alice pleaded, her commands broken and halting.

lines.japanese: 「男は言った、殺すナリタを」
lines.english: “Man say... kill Narita.”

lines.japanese: 「なに？　おい、なんだって！？」
lines.english: “What? Hey—what did she say!?”

lines.japanese: 俺は呼吸さえ忘れそうになったが、警官がアリスの腕を掴んだのを見てその手を払いとばした。
lines.english: I nearly forgot to breathe, but then the officer grabbed Alice’s arm. I slapped his hand away.

lines.japanese: 「どんな男だった」
lines.english: “What did the man look like?”

lines.japanese: 「私は見ていない。彼はかくしていた、顔を、ぼうしで」
lines.english: “I didn’t see. He hide face with hat.”
“With a hat...!”

lines.japanese: 帽子で顔を隠した男。俺は何かに衝きうごかされて立ちあがった。
lines.english: A man with his face hidden by a hat. Something drove me to my feet.

lines.japanese: 何かに──久しく忘れていた感情に。
lines.english: Something—a feeling I had long forgotten.
“That... bastard...”

lines.japanese: 立ちくらみがして思わず目を閉じた。目蓋の裏が赤く染まっているように見えた。
lines.english: A wave of dizziness made me close my eyes. The darkness behind my lids seemed stained red.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ」
lines.english: “Dra.”

lines.japanese: 小さな手が俺の手に触れた。その冷たさで、俺は我に返った。
lines.english: A small hand touched mine. Its coldness brought me back to myself.

lines.japanese: 「アリス……」
lines.english: “Alice...”

lines.japanese: 俺はやつの手を握りかえした。両手で包みこんだ。それから暗い激情を押しかえすように笑ってみせた。
lines.english: I squeezed her hand in return and cradled it in both of mine. Then I smiled as if I could force the dark surge inside me back down.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとな……俺は大丈夫。もちろんマルチネスも大丈夫だ」
lines.english: “Thanks... I'll be all right. And of course Martinez will be too.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえも大丈夫。お巡りさんが守ってくれる。家まで送ってもらって、帰ったら父ちゃんにぎゅってしてもらえ。それでぜんぶ大丈夫だ」
lines.english: “You'll be all right too. The police will protect you. Have them take you home, and when you get there, have your dad hold you tight. Then everything will be all right.”

lines.japanese: そう言って、アリスの柔らかいブロンドを真上からくしゃくしゃと撫でてやった。
lines.english: Saying that, I reached down and mussed her soft blond hair.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、こいつ頼んます」
lines.english: “Take care of her for me.”

lines.japanese: 「え……あ、おい、君っ！」
lines.english: “What...? Hey, wait!”

lines.japanese: 呼びとめる声を無視して、俺は見物人の壁が築かれていない車道側へと駆けだした。
lines.english: Ignoring the voice calling me back, I broke into a run toward the roadway, the only side where no wall of spectators had formed.

lines.japanese: 「待て！　おい、待ってくれ！　話を聞かせてもらわないと困る！」
lines.english: “Stop! Hey, wait! We need you to answer some questions!”

lines.japanese: 「こっちだって困んだよ、そんな余裕ねえっつの……！」
lines.english: “I’m in trouble too! I don’t have time for this...!”

lines.japanese: ガードレールを飛びこえ、ちらとだけ振りかえった。アリスが警官の腰に手を回して、引きとめるようにしがみついていた。
lines.english: I vaulted the guardrail and looked back only once. Alice had wrapped her arms around the officer's waist and clung to him, holding him back.

lines.japanese: 「任意だろ。なら断る！」
lines.english: “It's voluntary, isn't it? Then I refuse!”

lines.japanese: 俺は事情聴取の協力要請を拒否して、そのまま車道の端を路側帯に沿って走った。すぐ先の巨大な交差点で、幸いにも歩行者信号が青になった。俺は雑踏の行きかう横断歩道を駆けぬけた。
lines.english: I refused their request for voluntary questioning and kept running along the shoulder at the road’s edge. At the enormous intersection ahead, luckily, the pedestrian signal turned green. I raced through the stream of people in the crosswalk.

lines.japanese: 片側ニ車線の車道を渡って対岸に辿りつき、群衆の中に紛れこんだ。
lines.english: I crossed the four-lane road, reached the far side, and dissolved into the throng.

lines.japanese: アルバトロスの下では、多くのひとびとが何故だか頭上を仰いでいた。俺は歩を緩めながら、なんとはなしにそれに倣った。
lines.english: Beneath the Albatross, a great many people were looking overhead for reasons I couldn't guess. I slowed to a walk and, without really meaning to, followed their gaze.

lines.japanese: 駅舎に対峙する巨大な街頭ビジョンには、鏡像のように柳木原の街並が映しだされていた。
lines.english: On the giant street screen facing the station, the Yanagihara cityscape appeared like a mirror image.

lines.japanese: ニュースキャスターの感情を抑えた声が、夜の繁華街の一部として淡々と空に漂っていた。
lines.english: The news anchor’s restrained voice drifted impassively over the nighttime district, just another sound in the city.

lines.japanese: 「事件があったのは昨夜２２時過ぎ、柳木原駅東口前の大型ショッピングビル『アルバトロス』付近の路上で──」
lines.english: “The incident occurred shortly after ten last night on the street near the Albatross, a major shopping complex outside the east exit of Yanagihara Station—”

lines.japanese: アルバトロスの壁面に、もうひとつのアルバトロスがそびえ立っていた。
lines.english: A second Albatross towered on the wall of the first.

lines.japanese: 手品のような光景に、思わず足を止めてスクリーンに見入る通行人が多かった。俺も立ちどまった。止まらざるを得なかった。
lines.english: The sight stopped countless passersby as though they were watching a magic trick. It stopped me too. I had no choice but to watch.

lines.japanese: ゆうべの２２時過ぎ、アルバトロスの下。それは俺とプラチナが並び、語り、笑って別れた場所に不吉なぐらい符合する。
lines.english: Shortly after ten last night. Beneath the Albatross. Time and place matched with sickening precision the spot where Platinum and I had stood together, talked, laughed, and parted.

lines.japanese: いまキャスターは事件と言った。事件があったと言った。縁起の悪い偶然だ。
lines.english: The anchor had said *incident*. Said something had happened. An ominous coincidence.

lines.japanese: 「目撃者の証言によりますと、大勢の通行人で賑わう中、とつぜんパンという大きな音が聞こえ、次の瞬間、男性がひとりうずくまるように倒れたということです」
lines.english: “According to witnesses, the street was crowded with pedestrians when a sudden loud bang was heard. The next moment, they saw a man crumple to the ground.”

lines.japanese: 「調べによると男性は美空区の自由業・江藤弘之さん２３歳で、江藤さんは急ぎ美空総合病院へ運ばれましたが、出血多量などにより二時間後に死亡しました──」
lines.english: “Police have identified the man as Hiroyuki Eto, twenty-three, a self-employed resident of Misora Ward. Mr. Eto was rushed to Misora General Hospital but died two hours later from blood loss and related complications—”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: なんだって……？
lines.english: What did he say...?

lines.japanese: なにを……言ってるんだ、こいつは……？
lines.english: What... the hell was that man talking about...?

lines.japanese: 俺は画面の中の眼鏡ヅラを睨みあげながら、しかし体から力が抜けるのを感じて信号の柱に寄りかかった。
lines.english: I glared up at the bespectacled face on the screen. Then I felt the strength drain from my body, and I leaned against the traffic-light pole.

lines.japanese: 「プラ……チナ……」
lines.english: “Pla... tinum...”

lines.japanese: それでも脚に力が入らず、そもそも立っていることの必要性が感じられず、俺の体はランプポストの頼りない細さを伝って滑りおちていった。
lines.english: My legs still would not support me. More than that, standing no longer seemed to serve any purpose. I slid down the pole, which seemed far too slender to hold me.

lines.japanese: 尻で着地して、俺はどこか──どこか途方もない遠くを眺めていた。
lines.english: I landed on my ass and stared somewhere—somewhere impossibly far away.

lines.japanese: 投げだした足に、中年女の通行人がつまずいてよろめいていった。振りかえった眼光と不快げなうなり声を浴びせられたから、俺はぼんやり脚を短く折りたたんだ。
lines.english: A middle-aged woman tripped over my outflung legs and stumbled away. She looked back with a glare and an irritated growl. Dazed, I drew my legs in.

lines.japanese: 鳴にもらった安全靴を引きよせると、それが踏んでいた下には赤黒い染みがこびりついていた──
lines.english: As I drew the safety shoes Naru had given me closer, I saw the dark red stain crusted beneath where one of them had rested—

lines.japanese: ──血痕。
lines.english: —blood.
“That bastard...”

lines.japanese: プラチナの器用な笑顔と、チューリップ帽の奥の非情な忍び笑いが、白い靄のかかった頭にのしかかる。
lines.english: Platinum's practiced smile and the merciless snicker from beneath the tulip hat bore down upon my mind through a white fog.

lines.japanese: 俺は久しく忘れていた感情が、奈落の底のように奥深いところから這いのぼってくるのを感じた。
lines.english: I felt an emotion long forgotten crawling up from a place as deep as the bottom of an abyss.
“That... goddamn bastard...”

lines.japanese: 首の後ろに鈍い痛みが走る。視界がかすむ。音が遠ざかる。
lines.english: A dull pain shot through the back of my neck. My vision clouded. Sound withdrew into the distance.

lines.japanese: 浮遊感……重力が逆巻くように、頭が方々へ引っぱられる感覚。揺れる、風に揺れる。どこかで誰かが嗤っている。
lines.english: A floating sensation... Gravity seemed to churn in reverse, tugging my head every which way. I swayed. Swayed in the wind. Somewhere, someone was laughing.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth.*

lines.japanese: 「許せねえ……赦せるかよ……」
lines.english: “I can't forgive him... How the hell could I...?”

lines.japanese: 俺はてのひらに爪を食いこませた。
lines.english: I drove my nails into my palms.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。世界が平和でありますように。世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth.* *May peace prevail on Earth.* *May peace prevail on Earth.*

lines.japanese: 「ブッ殺す……ブッ殺すぞクソヤロウ……！」
lines.english: “I'll kill him... I'll fucking kill that bastard...!”

lines.japanese: ──じいさん。
lines.english: —Old man.

lines.japanese: なあ、じいさん。教えてくれよ。俺、馬鹿だから忘れちゃったよ。
lines.english: Hey, old man. Tell me. I'm an idiot. I've forgotten.

lines.japanese: 喚きたいのに、叫びたいのに、怒鳴りちらしたいのに……どうして俺は、こんなときでさえも堪えなきゃならないんだっけ。
lines.english: I wanted to howl, to scream, to roar until my throat tore... Why did I have to hold it in, even then? What was the reason again?

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように！
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth!*

lines.japanese: 「──ってえな、なまくら坊主っ！」
lines.english: “That hurt, you useless priest!”

lines.japanese: じいさんは、じいさんのくせに、じいさんとは思えない一発でいつもあっけなく俺に膝を折らしめた。
lines.english: Old man or not, he always buckled my knees with one effortless punch no old man should have been able to throw.

lines.japanese: 「ふむ……男同士の付き合いにゃあ、ときには示威行動が求められるかもしれん。とくに若いうちは意地や面子もあるだろう。それは分かるがな坊主、しかしだ、力ではなーんも解決せんぞ？」
lines.english: “Hmm... Between men, a show of force may sometimes seem necessary. Especially when you're young—you have your pride, your face to save. I understand that, son. But listen: force doesn't solve a blessed thing.”

lines.japanese: 「てめいま、おもくそ暴力ふるったろが！　説得力ねえんだよ！」
lines.english: “You just beat the living shit out of me! That speech doesn't carry much weight!”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、その憤りがなによりの証じゃないか。力ずくで言を封じても遺恨が残る。おまえはいま、俺を殴りかえしたいと思っているだろう」
lines.english: “No, no. Your outrage proves my point better than anything. Silence a man by force and the grievance remains. Right now, you want to hit me back, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 「ったりめえだ！」
lines.english: “No shit!”

lines.japanese: 俺は立ちあがると同時にこぶしを固めて飛びかかった。
lines.english: The instant I regained my feet, I clenched my fist and sprang at him.

lines.japanese: だが、やつは迎撃の右を振りおろして、ふたたび俺を教会の硬い床に沈めた。
lines.english: But he met me with a chopping right and sent me back to the church’s hard floor.

lines.japanese: 「怒りは怒りを呼び、憎しみは憎しみを膨らませる。怨嗟の輪は際限なくその半径を増してゆくだけだ。どこかで誰かが断ちきらねばならん……たしかに、それはとても難しいことなんだが」
lines.english: Anger summons anger, and hatred swells hatred. The circle of resentment only widens without end. Somewhere, someone must break the cycle... Of course, that's very hard to do.

lines.japanese: 「クソジジイ……」
lines.english: “Goddamn old man...”

lines.japanese: 難しいとか易しいとかの問題じゃない。不条理だ。俺はそう思った。
lines.english: This was not about hard or easy. It made no damn sense. That was what I thought.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ俺にどうしろっつんだよ！」
lines.english: “Then what the hell am I supposed to do?”

lines.japanese: 立ちあがることを諦め、俺は地べたの上で両手両足を広げた。
lines.english: Giving up on standing, I sprawled across the floor with all four limbs flung wide.

lines.japanese: 「タカシも鷲介もすぐ逃げる！　困ったときは必ず俺が担ぎだされンだ！」
lines.english: “Takashi and Shusuke run away the second anything happens! Whenever there's trouble, I'm the one they drag out!”

lines.japanese: 「今日だってそうだ、俺が≪コックピット≫に入ったらいきなり敵に囲まれてる！　やるしかねえだろ、他にどうしろっつんだ！　ジジイ、説教だったら俺じゃなくあの軟弱コンビにかましとけや！」
lines.english: “Today was the same! I step into the *Cockpit* and suddenly we’re surrounded by enemies! What else can I do but fight? What the hell else am I supposed to do? Old man, if you want to preach, preach at those two spineless cowards!”

lines.japanese: 「ふむ……まあ、そうだな……うむ、分かった、彼らにも追々それは」
lines.english: “Hmm... Well, yes... Yes, I see. I'll speak to them in due course—”

lines.japanese: 「しかし、ひとまず今日のところはおまえさんだ、隼人……山上の垂訓は知っているかな。『汝の敵を愛し、迫害する者のために祈れ』」
lines.english: “For today, however, we're dealing with you, Hayato... Do you know the Sermon on the Mount? ‘Love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you.’”

lines.japanese: それは、じいさんのしばしば口にする奇麗事だった──愛せ。祈れ。赦せ。
lines.english: It was the kind of pretty sentiment the old man often spouted—love them. Pray for them. Forgive them.

lines.japanese: 「ふざけんなよ、てめぇ。迫害されて愛せだァ？　マゾかっつうの」
lines.english: “Go screw yourself. They persecute me and I'm supposed to love them? What am I, a masochist?”

lines.japanese: 「はは、これはそう直截的な意味ではないんだよ。ここで言う愛とは、必ずしも親愛や友愛を指すものではなく、アガペーとも言うべき……いや、ううむ、そうだな、誤解を恐れず噛みくだいて言うなら──」
lines.english: “Ha ha. It isn’t meant quite so directly. The love here need not be affection or friendship, but something closer to the Greek *agape*... No, hmm. At the risk of oversimplifying, let me put it plainly—”

lines.japanese: 「──嫌いなものは嫌いでいい。ただ、おまえがおのずから手を下さずとも、嫌なやつや悪いやつにはいずれ天罰がくだる。だから復讐だの制裁だのという物騒なことは、天におわす神様に任せてしまえということだ」
lines.english: “—you may go right on hating someone. The point is, you need not raise a hand yourself. Sooner or later, the people you hate and the people who do evil will face divine punishment. Leave dangerous business like vengeance and retribution to God in Heaven.”

lines.japanese: 「どうだ。そう考えると、おまえの蛮行が馬鹿らしくならないか？　人間がわざわざ手を──同時に心を──汚す必要はないということなんだぞ」
lines.english: “Well? Looked at that way, doesn’t your savagery begin to seem foolish? A person needn’t go out of his way to soil his hands—and his heart.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ！　気休めとしちゃ悪くねえと思うけどな。でも所詮は理想論だろ、そんなん」
lines.english: “Hah! Not bad as comfort goes. But it's still pie in the sky.”

lines.japanese: 「さすがだよ。さすがはあんた、聖職者さまだよ。こんな清らかな部屋にこもって、ろくに世間を知らねーからそんなこと言えちゃうんだよバーカ。あんな？　あんたらとは違って、下々はそーゆーわけいかねーの！」
lines.english: “Of course. That’s our holy man for you. You shut yourself away in this spotless room and know nothing about the real world, so you can spout that crap, idiot. Listen, unlike you people, those of us down here don’t have that luxury!”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　そんなことはないぞ？　逆に言えば、おまえだってこの部屋の実情など知る由もあるまい？」
lines.english: “Hm? That isn't true. Turn it around: you have no way of knowing what really happens in this room, do you?”

lines.japanese: やつは俺を見下ろしながら、子供みたいに目を丸くして首を傾けた。
lines.english: He looked down at me, widened his eyes like a child, and tipped his head.

lines.japanese: 「ここだけの話だがな。聖職者？　いやいや、俺たちだって所詮は人間だ。むしろ、おまえさんらよりよっぽど弱い人間だ。なにしろ、神様なんてものに救いを求めて寄りあつまってくるような人種だからな」
lines.english: “Between you and me, now. Holy men? No, no. We’re only human too. If anything, we’re much weaker than the likes of you. After all, we’re the sort who gather together seeking salvation in this thing called God.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 下から見上げたじいさんの皺だらけの顔が、急に威厳を欠いて年老いたように見えた。
lines.english: Seen from below, the old man's wrinkled face abruptly lost its dignity. He simply looked old.

lines.japanese: 「弱い人間と一口に言っても、そこにはいろいろな弱さがある。だから、弱い人間同士で集まっていながら、その中でまた派閥ができる。派閥と派閥は互いを牽制する。そして──」
lines.english: “There are many kinds of weakness. So even when weak people gather, factions form among them. Each faction checks the other. And then—”

lines.japanese: 「──どの派閥にも入れず、両者の板ばさみになって潰れてゆく者もいる」
lines.english: “—some belong to neither side, are caught between the two, and are crushed.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえらと何も変わらんのだよ。ここは天国じゃない。俺たちは天使じゃない。俺たちの住む地上に、そんな場所ありはしないんだ。あ、いや……」
lines.english: “We're no different from you. This isn't Heaven. We aren't angels. No such place exists anywhere on this earth. Ah, no...”

lines.japanese: やつは気まずげに顎髭の中で言葉を呑みこんで、銀色の後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。
lines.english: He swallowed the rest of his words into his beard, then awkwardly scratched the silver hair at the back of his head.

lines.japanese: 「失言だな。まったく、おまえの言うとおり、俺はとんだなまくら坊主だ。さて、話を戻そう」
lines.english: Slip of the tongue. You're right; I'm one sorry excuse for a priest. Anyway, back to the story.

lines.japanese: じいさんが床の上に直接どすんと腰を落として、俺の正面にあぐらをかいた。俺は片膝を立てて上半身を引いた。
lines.english: The old man dropped heavily onto the bare floor and sat cross-legged in front of me. I leaned back and raised one knee.

lines.japanese: 「……んだよ。もう説教はええっつーの」
lines.english: “...What now? I told you, I've had enough sermons.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、そう構えなさんな。説教なんて大層なもんじゃない……こいつぁ、お爺さんの知恵袋だ」
lines.english: “No, no. Don't bristle. This is hardly grand enough to call a sermon... Think of it as a little wisdom from an old man.”

lines.japanese: 「さっきおまえは、主の教えを気休めだと言ったな。うむ、しかり……いまのおまえに必要なのは、使徒の伝えのこした福音なんぞよりも、気休めじみた暗示の呪文なのかもしれん」
lines.english: “A moment ago, you called the Lord's teaching mere comfort. Quite so... Perhaps what you need now, more than any gospel handed down by the apostles, is a comforting little incantation.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「そして信仰に恃まないおまえは、それを福音に縁る必要がない。要は暗示にすがることで心を平静に保てればいいんだからな」
lines.english: “And since you place no faith in religion, you need not tie it to the Gospel. All that matters is that you cling to the suggestion and keep your mind calm.”

lines.japanese: 「暗示ぃ？」
lines.english: “Self-suggestion?”

lines.japanese: 「そう。心が怒りや憎しみによって染まりそうなとき、それを制するための暗示、呪文、気休め……」
lines.english: “Yes. When anger or hatred threatens to stain your heart, a suggestion to hold it back. A spell. A comforting thought...”

lines.japanese: じいさんは言葉を止め、考えこむように腕を組んだ。ゆっくりと首をひねった。片側の頬が内側から突かれてぼこりと膨らんだ。
lines.english: The old man fell silent and folded his arms in thought. Slowly, he cocked his head. One cheek bulged as his tongue prodded it from within.

lines.japanese: 「おお、たとえばこんなのはどうだ。“女が百人降ってきますように”」
lines.english: “Oh! How about this, for example: ‘May a hundred women rain down from the sky.’”

lines.japanese: 「ふざけてんのか？」
lines.english: “Are you screwing with me?”

lines.japanese: 「ふん、つまらん小僧だ。もっと冗句をたしなむ男でないと女にはもてんぞ」
lines.english: “Hmph. What a dull boy. A man needs a better appreciation of jokes if he expects women to like him.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむ。ならこうしよう。文字通り器のでかいおまえさんらにぴったりの、でっかいでっかいお願いごとだ」
lines.english: “Hmm. Then let’s try this. A great big wish, perfect for a man with room for so many inside him.”

lines.japanese: 「……なんだよそれ」
lines.english: “...What's that supposed to be?”

lines.japanese: 「“世界が平和でありますように”」
lines.english: “*May peace prevail on Earth.*”

lines.japanese: 「はああ？」
lines.english: “Huuuuh?”

lines.japanese: 「ははは！　どうだ世界だ！　世界、こいつはスケールがでかいだろう！」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! The world, boy! The whole world! Now that's a grand scale, wouldn't you say?”

lines.japanese: 「世界が平和でありますように！　いいか隼人。赦しがたい敵に出会ったらそう唱えて、何度でもそう唱えて、必死で心を平静に保ちなさい。さもなければおまえは──」
lines.english: “*May peace prevail on Earth!* Listen, Hayato. When you meet an enemy you cannot forgive, recite those words. Recite them as often as it takes, and fight with all you have to keep your heart at peace. Otherwise, you will—”

lines.japanese: 「さもなければ……」
lines.english: “Otherwise...”

lines.japanese: 「さもなけりゃなんだっつんだよ、あァっ！？」
lines.english: “Otherwise what, damn it!?”

lines.japanese: 俺は立ちあがると同時に駆けだしていた。
lines.english: I was upright and running in the same instant.

lines.japanese: 久しく忘れていた感情が頭をもたげていた。
lines.english: An emotion I had long forgotten was raising its head.

lines.japanese: 「赦さねえ！　赦さねえ、あのオウム頭……ブッ殺す……ブッ殺すぞクソヤロウ！」
lines.english: “I won't forgive him! I won't forgive that parrot-headed bastard... I'll kill him... I'll fucking kill him!”

lines.japanese: 眩暈がするほどに叫んだ俺を──どこかで誰かが嗤っていた。
lines.english: Someone, somewhere was laughing as I screamed until my head swam.

lines.japanese: まるで内なる奈落から囁かれているようだった。
lines.english: The laughter seemed to whisper from an abyss inside me.

lines.japanese: “汝の敵を裁け”
lines.english: Pass judgment upon thine enemy.
